featured_reviews.review_text:
I was recommended the 12 week plan, as opposed to my originally intended 6 weeks.  I engaged for 5.5 weeks before quitting & had lost 4 KG’s during this. My experience was unpleasant for the most part, but my decision to opt for his plan recommendation - a real Blunder!

Having duped by of at-least Rs. 3000 (because he refused to refund) I believe it is my responsibility to convey my experience so that you (the reader) can re-consider your decision using valid data-points.

Pros -

➕ Makes tall claims in the intro discussion about the progress one can anticipate when following his program. This will give you the initial momentum & confidence to commence your journey on a very strong note.

Cons-

➖ Unprofessional - Right from the beginning, he would not stick to his own estimated delivery timelines for the program & diet delivery. And this continued through all the 5 weeks of my engagement where he had a revised program to deliver. Sometimes he would fail/forget to respond and will come with an excuse.

➖ Inexperienced when it comes to workout programming - His workout plans, exercise cues do not have any scientific basis to them. He doesn’t explain the decisions behind them even upon multiple requests. If you try to improvise his plans by providing feedback and/or ask questions in order to steering him and your journey in a more optimal direction, he would simply refuse. He would also advise you to not read/follow information from the internet citing everything as inaccurate except his advice.  Initially, I had the impression of him just being lazy but later when he dismissed my request to include compound movements in my routine even after 4 weeks and put me on a back-burner stating “Why would we even need compound movements?”, I realised that I became victim to an imbecile coach. In none of the weeks, did I find inclusion of the Big 3 (Squats, Benchpress & Deadlifts using barbell). These exercises require a proper warmup paradigm and since there was never any instructions on how to those. Not once, did he talk or mention about how to progressively overload.

➖ Copy-pasted exercises/routines - I would often find that some of the exercises stated in his routine would not have a valid name that is identifiable when googling. Sometimes, the exercises that were given would feel out of place for a morbidly-obese person. In one of the weeks where-in I had requested to include cardio in the revised routine, the routine that he delivered comprised of 5-6 randomly picked YouTube workouts of an hour or a little beyond. This shocked me beyond belief and was the final nail in the coffin in our mutual pursuit.

➖ Stalled progress - The reason why one opts for a trainer is so that progress is consistent throughout the journey.

➖ No form check - He didn’t request for videos to check if the move is being performed appropriately and with paramount importance given to safety. This in my opinion is extremely essential for a beginner lifter as injuries can not just derail your progress but also can give you a lifetime of agony (in adverse cases). Most online trainers do offer this as part of their service but not Pravin.

When following a plan diligently and giving 2x more effort, it is natural for a client to question when they hit a plateau (both inch loss & weight loss for 2 straight weeks) When I did so, he counter-stated that I am not counting calories by measuring food. As obvious as this cause might seem, I can safely say that it was an unintelligent & useless response because his allegation was baseless. I was expending 2x more while being in exact same diet & deficit.

Later, he alleged that I am stubborn & think that my knowledge exceeds his expertise.

For anyone reading this, I urge you to get the book "Bigger Leaner Stronger" by Michael Matthews.

Final Remarks -
